title: Emergent Model Probe & Fallback Trigger Playbook
creator: Ava Montgomery
description: Create an operational playbook that codifies how Product and Platform respond to the emergence of new model variants (open or third-party) that materially affect latency/cost/quality trade-offs for enterprise customers. The deliverable should include: detection probes, prioritization criteria, automated vs. manual fallback triggers, guardrails for private deployments, and a comms template for customers and sales.
background: We observed multiple signal spikes in external model availability over the last 6 months (benchmarks and customer reports). Current ad-hoc switches created inconsistent latency/cost outcomes for Dedicated and Private customers. This playbook reduces decision latency, minimizes churn risk, and harmonizes platform fallback behavior with PM/SE guidance.

decisions: Automatic fallback will be allowed for Hosted products under strict thresholds (latency increase >30% or cost per token >1.5x for 15 minutes).
Dedicated customers must opt into auto-fallback; default behavior is notify + manual approval for model switch.
Use a three-tier alert severity model: Info (catalog change), Elevated (compatibility risk detected), Critical (quality regression detected via eval set).
tradeoffs: Automated fallback reduces downtime but increases risk of subtle semantic regressions — mitigated by short canary window and automatic rollback rule
Conservative default for Dedicated minimizes surprise for enterprise customers but increases manual effort for SRE/product teams
Tighter thresholds reduce false positives but delay switches that could save cost or improve latency
